Start verifying a number as a caller ID. Plivo sends a one-time passcode to the
number, by SMS or, with --channel call, by a voice call, and answers with a
verification_uuid. Finish with plivo voice caller-ids verify <verification_uuid>
--otp <code>. The passcode is valid for 15 minutes.

The number is in E.164; the + is added if you leave it off. A number rented from
Plivo needs no verification. Plivo does not verify Indian (+91) numbers: it
refuses before sending anything.

Usage:
  plivo voice caller-ids create <number> [flags]

Aliases:
  create, add

Examples:
  plivo voice caller-ids create +14155550100 --alias "front desk" --yes
  plivo voice caller-ids create +14155550100 --channel call --yes

Flags:
      --alias string        a name for the caller ID
      --channel string      how the passcode is sent: sms|call (Plivo's default: sms)
  -h, --help                help for create
      --subaccount string   the subaccount that gets the caller ID (its auth ID)

Global Flags:
      --dry-run            preview requests and local changes without sending or writing anything
      --log-level string   log level: debug|info|warn|error|none (default "warn")
      --no-color           disable colored output
  -o, --output string      output format: table|json|jsonl|yaml|csv (default: table for TTY, json otherwise)
      --profile string     named profile from ~/.plivo/config.toml
      --query string       JMESPath filter on the JSON output, e.g. 'data.objects[].call_uuid' (implies -o json)
  -q, --quiet              suppress non-data output
      --schema             describe the command (arguments, flags, output fields) instead of running it
      --show-secrets       show auth tokens and passwords in API responses instead of [REDACTED]
      --timeout duration   request timeout: seconds, or a duration such as 90s or 2m (default 30s)
  -y, --yes                skip confirmation prompts
